emperor-alexander.heading: ALEXANDER
emperor-alexander.flavour: Flesh nearly white with faint yellow tinge, firm, coarse, moderately crisp, tender, juicy, mild subacid, fair to good.
emperor-alexander.quality: medium to good in quality, suitable for culinary rather than for dessert use
emperor-alexander.storage: It may be held in cold storage till November. It goes down quickly and as it does not stand heat well before going into storage it should be shipped the day it is picked and under ice.
emperor-alexander.note: Beach's synonyms include Emperor Alexander, Kaiser Alexander, Empereur Alexandre and Aporta; typical variety of the Russian Aport group. Same lines also recorded for aport.

aport.heading: ALEXANDER
aport.flavour: Flesh nearly white with faint yellow tinge, firm, coarse, moderately crisp, tender, juicy, mild subacid, fair to good.
aport.quality: medium to good in quality, suitable for culinary rather than for dessert use
aport.storage: It may be held in cold storage till November. It goes down quickly
aport.note: Beach lists Aporta as a synonym of Alexander (our aka Aport Alexander) and calls Alexander the typical variety of the Aport group (short note at line 570). He also describes a separate Aport Orient (syn. Aport, Budd's No. 252, line 586), 'resembles Alexander closely', ripening mid-August and 'coarse-grained and inferior in quality'. Same lines as emperor-alexander; identity with the Almaty Aport not certain.

antonovka.heading: ANTONOVKA
antonovka.flavour: flesh yellow, juicy, sprightly spicy subacid, good.
antonovka.quality: A Russian fruit of no practical value for this state.
antonovka.note: Short entry quoting Hansen's description; synonyms Antonowka, Antony, 26 M. Season given as October.

beauty-of-kent.heading: BEAUTY OF KENT
beauty-of-kent.quality: Fruit large, beautiful, showy, suitable for culinary use
beauty-of-kent.climate: In England where it originated it is said to do best under garden culture in warm soil and on Paradise stock; grown in clay and other uncongenial soils it loses quality.
beauty-of-kent.note: Short entry; season late September to November. Leroy gives Kentish Pippin as a synonym (not our colonel-vaughan).

bismarck.heading: BISMARCK
bismarck.flavour: Flesh nearly white, moderately firm, coarse, rather tender, juicy, subacid, sprightly, fair to good or nearly good.
bismarck.quality: suitable for kitchen and market purposes but inferior in dessert qualities
bismarck.storage: its season extends from October to early winter
bismarck.note: Beach gives the origin as the Province of Canterbury, New Zealand (our record says Australia). Related to the Aport group; ranks with Alexander and Wolf River in quality.

blenheim-orange.heading: BLENHEIM
blenheim-orange.flavour: Flesh tinged with yellow, rather firm, moderately juicy, crisp, moderately fine grained or a little coarse, somewhat aromatic, agreeable sprightly subacid, becoming rather mild subacid, good to very good; excellent either for dessert or culinary use.
blenheim-orange.quality: attractive in appearance and of excellent quality
blenheim-orange.storage: It is at its best from October to December but often may be kept until midwinter or later.
blenheim-orange.note: Described as Blenheim; synonyms Blenheim Orange, Blenheim Pippin, Woodstock Pippin. Beach notes it is not a good keeper and is variable in season.

magnum-bonum.heading: BONUM
magnum-bonum.flavour: Flesh white, often stained next to the skin, firm, fine, tender, juicy, aromatic, mild subacid, very good for dessert.
magnum-bonum.quality: a southern variety of very good quality when grown under favorable conditions
magnum-bonum.climate: Probably it is not well adapted to regions as far north as New York
magnum-bonum.note: Described as Bonum with synonym Magnum Bonum; origin Davidson county, N. C. Fruit description compiled from other authors.

belle-de-boskoop.heading: BOSKOOP
belle-de-boskoop.flavour: the texture is somewhat coarse, and the flavor rather too acid for an agreeable dessert apple, but late in the season its acidity becomes modified. Flesh tinged with yellow, firm, somewhat coarse, tender, juicy, crisp, brisk subacid, good to very good.
belle-de-boskoop.quality: more suitable for general market and culinary purposes than for dessert
belle-de-boskoop.storage: As grown in Western New York generally some of the fruit may be kept till April.
belle-de-boskoop.climate: When grown on warm soils in Southern New York it may be marketed in September, but in the more northern regions of the state it keeps into the winter.
belle-de-boskoop.note: Synonyms Belle de Boskoop, Schoner von Boskoop, Reinette Monstrueuse.

catshead.heading: CATHEAD
catshead.flavour: Fruit very large, pale green, subacid.
catshead.note: Short entry; synonyms Catshead, Catshead Greening, Tete de Chat; Floy-Lindley's Costard and Emmons's Costard Ray are also listed as synonyms (our costard not recorded).

coxs-orange-pippin.heading: COX ORANGE
coxs-orange-pippin.flavour: Flesh yellow, firm, nearly fine, crisp, tender, very juicy, rich, sprightly subacid or becoming mild subacid, decidedly aromatic, very good to best.
coxs-orange-pippin.quality: One of the best in quality of the English dessert apples
coxs-orange-pippin.storage: in season from late September to early winter
coxs-orange-pippin.note: Beach drops the possessive: Cox Orange = Cox's Orange Pippin.

early-harvest.heading: EARLY HARVEST
early-harvest.flavour: Flesh white, not firm, rather fine, crisp, tender, juicy, at first briskly subacid but eventually becoming milder, and more agreeable for dessert. Good to very good.
early-harvest.storage: it keeps but a short time
early-harvest.note: Synonyms include Yellow Harvest, July Pippin, Prince's Harvest and Tart Bough (of some). Beach's separate Tart Bough (line 12870) is a different, more acid variety.

fall-pippin.heading: FALL PIPPIN
fall-pippin.flavour: The flesh is tender, rich and very good in quality. Flesh whitish or tinged with yellow, moderately firm, rather fine, tender, very juicy, agreeable subacid, somewhat aromatic, very good.
fall-pippin.quality: excellent for dessert but especially desirable for culinary uses
fall-pippin.storage: even carefully selected fruit cannot be relied upon to hold in common storage till December 1st without considerable loss. In cold storage it may be held till January or February.
fall-pippin.note: The OCR lost the heading and references (page 61); the entry starts at its SYNONYMS line, which includes Pound Pippin. Beach compares it with Holland Pippin.

gladstone.heading: GLADSTONE
gladstone.flavour: Flesh slightly tinged with yellow, moderately firm, a little coarse, crisp, tender, juicy, mild subacid, fair in quality.
gladstone.quality: It is not equal to either of these varieties in quality.
gladstone.note: Synonym Mr. Gladstone; intermediate in appearance between Oldenburg and Gravenstein, inferior to both in quality.

gravenstein.heading: GRAVENSTEIN
gravenstein.flavour: Flesh yellowish, firm, moderately fine, crisp, moderately tender, juicy, sprightly subacid, aromatic, very good to best.
gravenstein.quality: an apple of good size, attractive appearance and excellent quality. For culinary purposes it is perhaps unexcelled by any variety of its season.
gravenstein.storage: When properly handled a considerable portion of the fruit may remain apparently sound much later than this but the color fades and the quality and flavor deteriorate.
gravenstein.climate: In many sections of the state the tree is regarded as not quite hardy, being somewhat subject to sunscald and canker.

hawthornden.heading: HAWTHORNDEN
hawthornden.flavour: Flesh mild subacid, not of high flavor, pleasant, good.
hawthornden.climate: A Scotch variety which has done fairly well in various parts of this country from New England to California.
hawthornden.note: Beach had not grown it; description is second-hand. Lists Hawley as an erroneous synonym (his Hawley, line 5663, is a different American apple).

kentish-fillbasket.heading: KENTISH FILLBASKET
kentish-fillbasket.flavour: Flesh whitish, firm, moderately coarse, crisp, rather tender, juicy, brisk subacid, good.
kentish-fillbasket.quality: desirable for cooking but not for dessert use
kentish-fillbasket.note: Synonyms Lady de Grey's, Potter's Large. Following Hogg, the Kentish Fillbasket of Miller and Forsyth is a different apple (the old English Codlin).

keswick-codlin.heading: KESWICK
keswick-codlin.flavour: Flesh nearly white, fine, tender, very juicy, brisk subacid, good for culinary use, too acid for dessert unless very ripe.
keswick-codlin.quality: particularly esteemed on account of its excellence for culinary use
keswick-codlin.storage: It is not adapted for storage, its commercial limit in ordinary storage being September and early October.
keswick-codlin.note: Described as Keswick, synonym Keswick Codlin; distinct from the English Codling of Coxe and Forsyth.

landsberger-reinette.heading: LANDSBERG
landsberger-reinette.flavour: pleasant subacid flavor. Flesh nearly white, very tender, crisp, rather fine-grained, mild subacid, agreeable in flavor, good to very good for dessert.
landsberger-reinette.quality: a good dessert apple but less desirable for culinary uses because when it is cooked it lacks character in texture, color and flavor
landsberger-reinette.storage: Some of the fruit keeps apparently sound till March or later but after January it loses in quality.
landsberger-reinette.note: Described as Landsberg, synonym Landsberger Reinette; raised about 1840 by Mr. Burkhardt at Landsberg.

lord-suffield.heading: LORD SUFFIELD
lord-suffield.flavour: flesh white, rather fine, moderately juicy, subacid, good for culinary use.
lord-suffield.quality: considered by some one of the best apples of the group
lord-suffield.storage: suitable for cooking as early as the middle of July and remains in use till September
lord-suffield.note: Keswick Codlin group; blighted badly at Geneva.

mcintosh-red.heading: McINTOSH
mcintosh-red.flavour: The flesh is very tender, perfumed and delicious. Flesh white or slightly tinged with yellow, sometimes veined with red, firm, fine, crisp, tender, very juicy, characteristically and agreeably aromatic, perfumed, sprightly, subacid, becoming mild and nearly sweet when very ripe, very good to best for dessert.
mcintosh-red.quality: very good to best for dessert
mcintosh-red.storage: In Western New York it cannot be expected to keep much later than October in ordinary storage without considerable loss but in cold storage it may be held until December or January.
mcintosh-red.climate: When grown in more northern or elevated regions it is often held in good condition till midwinter or later.

american-mother.heading: MOTHER
american-mother.flavour: tender, rich, aromatic flesh of best dessert quality. It is less desirable for culinary uses, being somewhat lacking in acidity. Flesh fine, tender, juicy, very mild subacid, aromatic, very good to best in flavor and quality.
american-mother.storage: In ordinary storage it does not keep well and November is its safe commercial limit, but in cold storage it may be held till March or later.
american-mother.climate: In many localities it is rather tender and liable to scald or canker on the trunk and larger branches.
american-mother.note: Described as Mother; synonyms American Mother, Gardener's Apple, Mother of America. Resembles Esopus Spitzenburg.

duchess-of-oldenburg.heading: OLDENBURG
duchess-of-oldenburg.flavour: Flesh tinged with yellow, rather firm, moderately fine, crisp, tender, juicy, sprightly subacid, aromatic, good to very good for culinary purposes. It has too much acidity for a good dessert apple.
duchess-of-oldenburg.quality: good to very good for culinary purposes
duchess-of-oldenburg.storage: Since the fruit is quite perishable it does not stand heat well before shipment and goes down rather quickly
duchess-of-oldenburg.climate: The tree is highly valued because of its great hardiness.
duchess-of-oldenburg.note: Beach uses the A.P.S. name Oldenburg (cross-reference under Duchess of Oldenburg at line 3064); synonyms Duchess, Charlamowsky, Borowitsky. His Borovinka (line 1614) is treated as distinct.

peasgoods-nonsuch.heading: PEASGOOD NONSUCH
peasgoods-nonsuch.note: Short entry; little tested in America.

coxs-pomona.heading: POMONA
coxs-pomona.flavour: Flesh whitish, not very firm, rather fine, crisp, tender, juicy, subacid, sprightly, good to very good for culinary use.
coxs-pomona.quality: good to very good for culinary use
coxs-pomona.storage: not a very good keeper. In ordinary storage its commercial limit is October.
coxs-pomona.note: Described as Pomona, synonym Cox's Pomona; raised by Mr. Cox, who also raised Cox Orange.

red-astrachan.heading: RED ASTRACHAN
red-astrachan.flavour: Flesh white often strongly tinged with red, rather fine, crisp, tender, juicy, brisk subacid, aromatic, sometimes slightly astringent, good to very good.
red-astrachan.quality: When fully ripe and mellow it is desirable for dessert use.
red-astrachan.storage: It is very perishable, and on this account not well adapted for shipping to distant markets.
red-astrachan.note: Fit for culinary use before fully ripe.

ribston-pippin.heading: RIBSTON
ribston-pippin.flavour: Flesh tinged with yellow, firm, very crisp, medium in texture, juicy, pleasantly aromatic, rich, sprightly subacid, very good.
ribston-pippin.quality: much esteemed for its rich flavor and fine quality
ribston-pippin.storage: Heat ripens it quickly and it is not considered a very good keeper.
ribston-pippin.climate: It is not grown to any considerable extent in New York but succeeds better farther north, as in portions of Northern New England and of Canada
ribston-pippin.note: Described as Ribston; synonyms Ribston Pippin, Glory of York, Formosa Pippin, Travers. Same group as Hubbardston.

sops-in-wine.heading: SOPS OF WINE
sops-in-wine.flavour: Flesh yellowish often stained with pink, soft, fine, juicy, aromatic, mild, pleasant, subacid, good.
sops-in-wine.quality: Of little value except as a dessert apple for family use.
sops-in-wine.note: Synonyms Sops in Wine, Sapson, Rode Wyn Appel; quoted from Hogg as a very ancient English culinary and cider apple.

summer-rambo.heading: SUMMER RAMBO
summer-rambo.flavour: Flesh yellowish-green, firm, breaking, coarse, tender, very juicy, mildly subacid, somewhat aromatic, good.
summer-rambo.note: Synonyms Rambour Franc, Rambour d'Ete, Summer Rambour; said to have originated in France.

tom-putt.heading: TOM PUTT
tom-putt.flavour: A rather attractive red apple of good size, moderately coarse, subacid, fair to good for culinary uses.
tom-putt.quality: fair to good for culinary uses

twenty-ounce.heading: TWENTY OUNCE
twenty-ounce.flavour: Flesh whitish somewhat tinged with yellow, coarse, moderately tender, juicy, subacid, good for culinary use, second rate for dessert.
twenty-ounce.quality: good for culinary use, second rate for dessert
twenty-ounce.storage: In common storage the fruit goes down rapidly during October and November. In cold storage it may be kept till midwinter
twenty-ounce.climate: It seems to succeed particularly well in favorable locations in the apple belt south of Lake Ontario. It is especially subject to sunscald and canker on the trunk and larger limbs.
twenty-ounce.note: Synonyms Cayuga Red Streak, Eighteen Ounce; distinct from Twenty Ounce Pippin.

wealthy.heading: WEALTHY
wealthy.flavour: Flesh whitish sometimes stained with red, moderately fine, crisp, tender, very juicy, agreeable subacid, sprightly, somewhat aromatic, good to very good.
wealthy.quality: good in quality for either dessert or culinary uses
wealthy.storage: In ordinary storage its commercial limit is October, but in cold storage it may be kept till January or later.
wealthy.climate: This variety is particularly valuable for cold climates because the tree is very hardy

wolf-river.heading: WOLF RIVER
wolf-river.flavour: Flesh slightly tinged with yellow, firm, moderately coarse, tender, juicy, subacid, a little aromatic, fair to good.
wolf-river.storage: with October as the commercial limit in ordinary storage. In cold storage it may be held till January. It does not stand heat well, and goes down quickly
wolf-river.note: Aport group; supposed seedling of Alexander.

white-transparent.heading: YELLOW TRANSPARENT
white-transparent.flavour: Flesh white, moderately firm, fine-grained, crisp, tender, juicy, sprightly subacid with a pleasant but not high flavor, good or sometimes very good.
white-transparent.quality: excellent for culinary use and acceptable for dessert. It is not equal in quality to Early Harvest
white-transparent.climate: In some portions of the West it suffers from twig blight (fire blight) but it appears to be quite free from this disease in New York.
white-transparent.note: Described as Yellow Transparent; synonyms Transparente Jaune, Skwosnoi Schotoi; imported from Russia in 1870.

hyslop.heading: HYSLOP
hyslop.flavour: Flesh yellow, sometimes with tinge of red next the skin, very firm, moderately fine, at first juicy but eventually becoming dry and mealy, subacid, astringent, good for culinary purposes.
hyslop.storage: at first juicy but eventually becoming dry and mealy

siberian-crab.heading: RED SIBERIAN
siberian-crab.flavour: flesh subacid, astringent, good for culinary uses.
siberian-crab.note: Beach's Red Siberian has the synonym Siberian Crab (older authors); fruit three-quarters of an inch to an inch, ornamental, in clusters; origin given as France (Budd-Hansen). A cultivated form; our record is the species Malus baccata. Yellow Siberian (line 15689, also called Siberian Crab by Waring) is similar but golden.

transcendent.heading: TRANSCENDENT
transcendent.flavour: Flesh yellow, crisp, juicy, moderately fine, somewhat astringent, subacid, very good for culinary uses.
transcendent.note: Crabapple; in Prince's catalogue as early as 1844.

benoni.heading: BENONI
benoni.flavour: Flesh yellow, firm, crisp, fine-grained, tender, juicy, pleasant subacid, good to very good.
benoni.quality: Benoni is a fine dessert apple, very attractive in appearance and excellent in quality but not large enough to be a good market variety.
benoni.note: Originated in Dedham, Massachusetts; introduced shortly before 1832. Found by own search (no candidate line).

bietigheimer.heading: BETIGHEIMER
bietigheimer.flavour: It is a good cooking apple but coarse, subacid and not desirable for dessert use. Flesh almost white, firm, very coarse, crisp, somewhat tough, juicy, subacid, fair to nearly good.
bietigheimer.quality: Fruit remarkable only for its great size and beauty.
bietigheimer.note: Heading spelt Betigheimer; synonyms Bietigheimer, Red Bietigheimer. Origin Germany. Found by own search.

chenango.heading: CHENANGO
chenango.flavour: Flesh white, moderately firm, tender, juicy, mild subacid, very aromatic, good to very good.
chenango.quality: of excellent dessert quality and good also for culinary uses
chenango.storage: The latest ripening fruit may be kept in ordinary storage till November, but after that the color fades and it deteriorates much in quality, even though it may remain apparently sound (22).
chenango.note: Synonyms Chenango Strawberry, Sherwood's Favorite, Strawberry as in our aka.

detroit-red.heading: DETROIT RED
detroit-red.flavour: It is esteemed by many for dessert use because of its mild, pleasant flavor. Flesh white, sometimes streaked or stained with red, rather coarse, tender, juicy, agreeable mild subacid, very aromatic, good to very good.
detroit-red.storage: It is quite variable in keeping qualities, being commonly in season about with Maiden Blush.
detroit-red.note: Synonyms Detroit, Detroit Black, Black Detroit, Crimson Pippin as in our aka. Beach warns that Detroit Red and Detroit Black may be two or more varieties grown under these names in Western New York; he describes them as one. Supposed brought to Detroit by early French settlers.

gloria-mundi.heading: GLORIA MUNDI
gloria-mundi.flavour: Flesh slightly tinged with greenish-yellow, coarse, moderately crisp, rather tender, juicy, rather mild subacid, fair or nearly good in quality.
gloria-mundi.quality: fair or nearly good in quality
gloria-mundi.note: Synonyms American Mammoth, Monstrous Pippin, Glazenwood Gloria Mundi, Ox Apple, Pound as in our aka. Fruit of largest size, suitable only for culinary purposes.

golden-sweet.heading: GOLDEN SWEET
golden-sweet.flavour: Fruit of good medium size, attractive clear yellow when fully mature, rich, sweet, very good in flavor and quality. Flesh yellowish-white, firm, fine-grained, moderately tender, juicy, very sweet, aromatic, good to very good.
golden-sweet.quality: very good in flavor and quality
golden-sweet.note: Old Connecticut variety, mid-August to late September; synonyms Golden Sweeting and Early Golden Sweet match ours. Beach describes 'Summer Sweet' (another old Connecticut sweet apple, in our aka) as a separate variety, so that entry was not used.

american-golden-pippin.heading: GOLDING
american-golden-pippin.flavour: flesh rather coarse, aromatic, subacid and excellent in quality for either dessert or culinary uses.
american-golden-pippin.quality: excellent in quality for either dessert or culinary uses
american-golden-pippin.note: Described under Golding, with synonyms American Golden Pippin, American Golden, Golden Apple and Golden Pippin of Westchester County (all in our aka). Found by own search via Beach's note on 'The Golden Pippins'.

hibernal.heading: HIBERNAL
hibernal.flavour: flesh acid, with some astringency, juicy, good for cooking. Flesh yellowish, crisp, tender, juicy, acid; core small; quality above medium.
hibernal.quality: Although not a good dessert fruit this is a fine cooking apple and on account of its great hardiness and productiveness is one of the best of the Russian apples
hibernal.climate: A Russian variety which is proving valuable in portions of the Upper Mississippi valley and the Northwest because of its ability to withstand the rigorous climatic conditions of those regions.
hibernal.note: Flavour sentences are Beach's quotations of Hansen and Macoun. Synonyms Orsimui, Osimoe, Ronma (Romna) match ours; Beach describes Romna (Romenskoe) separately as a distinct Russian apple.

jefferis.heading: JEFFERIS
jefferis.flavour: Fruit of medium size, yellow, blushed and splashed with red; flesh tender, mild subacid, delicious. Flesh yellowish-white, firm, fine, crisp, tender, very juicy, mild subacid, very good.
jefferis.storage: It begins to ripen in September and continues in season till early winter. Commercial limit October (25).
jefferis.note: Synonyms Everbearing, Grantham as in our aka; Chester county, Pa., 1848.

liveland-raspberry.heading: LOWLAND RASPBERRY
liveland-raspberry.flavour: flesh white, often stained with red, fine, very tender, pleasant mild subacid, almost sweet
liveland-raspberry.note: Short note quoting Hansen; synonyms Liveland, Livland and Lievland Raspberry. Not tested in New York.

maiden-blush.heading: MAIDEN BLUSH
maiden-blush.flavour: The flesh is white, sprightly, not superior in flavor but good in quality. Flesh white or with slight yellow tinge, fine, moderately crisp, tender, very juicy, subacid, good in quality especially for culinary uses.
maiden-blush.quality: good in quality especially for culinary uses
maiden-blush.storage: Later than this although the fruit may appear sound it is deficient in quality. In cold storage its commercial limit appears to be about December 15th. It does not stand heat well before going into storage.
maiden-blush.note: Heading OCR 'MADDEN BLUSH'. Synonyms Lady Blush, Red Cheek as in our aka; described by Coxe in 1817, named by Samuel Allinson of Burlington, N.J.

ohio-nonpareil.heading: OHIO NONPAREIL
ohio-nonpareil.flavour: Flesh tinged with yellow, firm, moderately fine, crisp, tender, juicy, agreeable subacid, aromatic, good to very good.
ohio-nonpareil.quality: A fine fall apple of good color and good quality for either dessert or culinary purposes.
ohio-nonpareil.note: Synonyms Myers Nonpareil, Bellflower of the West, Cattell Apple, Rusty Core, Wells as in our aka; originated near Massillon, Ohio. Beach's vol. 1 'Wells' is a different (Maryland) apple.

primate.heading: PRIMATE
primate.flavour: the fruit ripens in succession during a period of several weeks and is of fine flavor and excellent quality particularly for dessert use. Flesh whitish, fine, crisp, very tender, juicy, subacid, aromatic, sprightly, very good to best.
primate.climate: In some localities the tree has proved somewhat tender, not very long-lived and rather susceptible to the attacks of the apple canker
primate.note: Synonyms July Apple, Powers, Scott, Early Tart Harvest, Sour Harvest, Rough and Ready as in our aka. Commonly considered the best apple of its season for the home orchard.

pumpkin-sweet.heading: PUMPKIN SWEET
pumpkin-sweet.flavour: By many it is esteemed as one of the best sweet apples of its season for baking and for canning or stewing with quinces, but generally it is not valued for dessert because it is rather coarse and has a peculiar flavor. Flesh tinged with yellow, firm, medium in texture, crispness and juiciness, decidedly sweet with a peculiar flavor; good for culinary use and especially esteemed for baking.
pumpkin-sweet.quality: good for culinary use and especially esteemed for baking
pumpkin-sweet.storage: Its keeping qualities differ greatly in different localities and in different seasons. The rate of loss in ordinary storage is usually high during the fall, and the season closes in December or early January
pumpkin-sweet.climate: It appears to thrive particularly well on well fertilized gravelly or sandy loam, with well drained subsoil.
pumpkin-sweet.note: Synonyms Pound Sweet, Lyman's Pumpkin Sweet, Pumpkin Sweeting, Vermont Pumpkin Sweet, Rhode Island Sweet as in our aka; Manchester, Conn. Beach notes other apples sold as Pumpkin Sweet are russeted or red; this one is green-yellow.

american-summer-pearmain.heading: SUMMER PEARMAIN
american-summer-pearmain.flavour: An amateur fruit which when perfect is beautiful and of mild, rich, excellent flavor (26). Flesh yellowish, very fine, tender, almost melting, juicy, aromatic, crisp, mild subacid, best.
american-summer-pearmain.note: Synonyms American Summer Pearmain, Early Summer Pearmain, American Pearmain, American Summer as in our aka; first described by Coxe 1817. Beach notes a different, later English Summer Pearmain.

sweet-bough.heading: SWEET BOUGH
sweet-bough.flavour: As a table apple, it will not rank as high as the Early Harvest; but, as a kitchen fruit, in its honied sweetness and tender flesh, it has no equal of its season. Flesh white, moderately firm, fine, somewhat crisp, very tender, juicy, sweet, slightly aromatic, good to very good.
sweet-bough.storage: It is handled to a limited extent in local markets, but is too soft to stand shipping to distant markets.
sweet-bough.climate: In unfavorable locations the tree is sometimes injured by winter
sweet-bough.note: The 'honied sweetness' sentence is Beach's quotation of Hovey. Synonyms Early Bough, Large Yellow Bough, August Sweet, Bough, Early Sweet Bough, Yellow Bough as in our aka.

williams-favourite.heading: WILLIAMS
williams-favourite.flavour: Williams is a very beautiful, bright red apple of mild agreeable flavor, good for dessert but not suitable for culinary uses. Flesh sometimes tinged with red, firm, a little coarse, moderately crisp, tender, rather juicy, becoming dry when overripe, pleasant mild subacid, aromatic, good.
williams-favourite.quality: good for dessert but not suitable for culinary uses
williams-favourite.storage: rather juicy, becoming dry when overripe
williams-favourite.note: Synonyms Williams Favorite, Williams Early Red, Williams Red, Queen, Lady's Apple as in our aka; Roxbury, Mass.

autumn-bough.heading: AUTUMN BOUGH.
autumn-bough.flavour: Flesh white, very tender, and with a rich and sweet, yet sprightly flavor.
autumn-bough.quality: regarded by many as one of the best sweet apples of its season for dessert use and is esteemed also for culinary purposes.
autumn-bough.storage: Ripens from 25th of Eighth month to the 20th of Ninth month.
autumn-bough.note: Synonyms Autumn Sweet Bough, Fall Bough, Late Bough, Montgomery Sweet, Philadelphia Sweet. Flavour and season are Parsons (1846) quoted by Beach. Hangs well but does not ship well.
